summary:
Outpost Gale is a browser game where kids can run a small research base at Gale crater on Mars, where NASA’s Curiosity rover explores. Players keep their crew alive by balancing three resources: Power, Life support and Crew health. They gather supplies on trips to real Curiosity sites, build upgrades that always help one thing and cost another, and seal a storm shelter against radiation at the cost of that night’s power. Earth’s forecasts arrive a day late, so players often decide before they know.

Every solar storm in the game is a real event from NASA’s DONKI database. Radiation levels come from Curiosity, fact cards come from NASA OSDR studies, and trip scenes show real Curiosity photos. Plain words, clear feedback and no game over make it friendly for young players. Instead of memorising space facts, kids feel the real trade-offs astronauts face, and learn that in space no choice is free.
details:
Outpost Gale is a browser game where players get to run a small research base on Mars. This base sits in Gale crater, the same place NASA’s Curiosity rover has been exploring since 2012. The goal is simple: keep the crew alive until the next crew lands. And to do this, players would need to juggle three main resources Power, Life support and Crew health.

Each Mars day (sol) gives the players 8 "hours" to spend on various decisions. You start inside the base, where a wall screens explain how everything works and a NASA News screen shows real space weather taken from the data provided. Then you head outside to real places Curiosity visited, like the Bagnold Dunes and Rocknest, to gather soil, water, parts and rock samples, paying for every trip in work time and radiation. Players would need to plan what resources they are looking for to build facilities to keep them alive. Back at base, you spend those supplies on upgrades, for each upgrade there are tradeoffs for users to consider. An oxygen maker refills the air, for example, but drains power every sol. A daily report explains how your resources have changed that day and why it does.

Some features and events in the game include: Life support runs down daily. Real solar storms hit at night, and sealing the Storm Shelter protects the crew but uses more power. Every machine running draws power, and dust storms cut solar in half. The greenhouse feeds the crew but needs power and can get sick crops. Earth’s forecast always arrives a sol late, so you often have to decide before you know. Every storm in the game is an actual solar particle event from NASA’s DONKI database, shown with its real date, and the title screen checks DONKI live for the Sun’s activity over the last 30 days. The radiation levels come from Curiosity’s RAD instrument, the fact cards come from real NASA OSDR studies, and the trip scenes use real Curiosity photos of each site.

In order to cater to a younger audience, a friendly robot called BOLT will explains each new word the first time it appears, key words are colour-coded, and every popup says why it appeared. There’s no game over: if things go wrong, you get an ending that explains what happened and what to try next. There are 2 different modes catering to what age the player is. Cadet mode uses easy words, Commander mode shows real units.

I built it in Unity with C# and exported it to WebGL so it runs in the browser. The game rules live in plain C# code separate from the visuals and are checked by 56 automated tests. A small Node.js script downloads and bundles the NASA data, keeping the source and date of every record. The characters were drawn by Python scripts, and the base buildings, icons and sounds come from Kenney’s free CC0 packs. SI has helped with the code and the drawing scripts, and the AI-assisted art is labelled in the game. The idea and design are my own.

My goal of this project is hope to help the younger generation understand the realities of harsh climate in space and that astronauts have to make critical decisions everyday sometimes without a complete idea of what is happening. I hope players learn something about Mars by living through some of the historical events and have as much fun as I did building this game :)
